source_refs.note: Exercise 3.4, Question 12: Exercise 3.4, book page 94: Q1-Q15 (integration by partial fractions); answers book pages 301-302

blocks.explanation:
Denominator mein do quadratic factors hain, \(x^2 + 1\) aur \(x^2 + 4\), dono irreducible (kabhi zero nahi hote) aur alag alag. Yeh Case-III hai.
Upar degree 3 aur neeche degree 4, is liye fraction proper hai.
Har quadratic factor ke upar linear numerator aayega, yani chaar constants. Koi real root nahi, is liye constants sirf coefficients compare kar ke milenge.
Plan: coefficients compare, phir har fraction ko ek \(\ln\) wale hisse aur ek \(\tan^{-1}\) wale hisse mein torna.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{x^3 + 2x + 1}{(x^2 + 1)(x^2 + 4)}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: yeh integral.
Tareeqa: Case-III do quadratic factors ke saath. Integral ke liye do formulas chahiye: \(\int \frac{2x}{x^2 + a^2}\,dx = \ln(x^2 + a^2)\) (upar neeche ka derivative hai) aur \(\int \frac{dx}{x^2 + a^2} = \frac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{a}\).

Partial fractions likhein
\[\dfrac{x^3 + 2x + 1}{(x^2 + 1)(x^2 + 4)} = \dfrac{Ax + B}{x^2 + 1} + \dfrac{Cx + D}{x^2 + 4}\]
\[x^3 + 2x + 1 = (Ax + B)(x^2 + 4)\]
\[+\, (Cx + D)(x^2 + 1)\]
Kyun: Har irreducible quadratic factor ke upar linear numerator. Phir poore denominator se multiply kiya.

Khol kar coefficients compare karein
\[x^3:\ A + C = 1\]
\[x^2:\ B + D = 0\]
\[x:\ 4A + C = 2\]
\[\text{constant}:\ 4B + D = 1\]
Kyun: \((Ax + B)(x^2 + 4) = Ax^3 + Bx^2 + 4Ax + 4B\) aur \((Cx + D)(x^2 + 1) = Cx^3 + Dx^2 + Cx + D\). Left side \(x^3 + 0x^2 + 2x + 1\) se milaya.
Dhyan dein: Left side mein \(x^2\) wala term nahi hai, is liye us ka coefficient 0 likhna zaroori hai.

Equations hal karein
\[3A = 1:\ A = \tfrac{1}{3},\ C = \tfrac{2}{3}\]
\[3B = 1:\ B = \tfrac{1}{3},\ D = -\tfrac{1}{3}\]
Kyun: \(x\) wali equation se \(x^3\) wali minus ki: \((4A + C) - (A + C) = 2 - 1\), yani \(3A = 1\). Isi tarah constant wali se \(x^2\) wali minus: \(3B = 1\). Phir \(C = 1 - A\) aur \(D = -B\).

Integrand nayi shakal mein
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{x + 1}{x^2 + 1} + \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{2x - 1}{x^2 + 4}\]
Kyun: Chaaron constants rakh kar \(\frac{1}{3}\) common nikal liya, taa ke fractions saaf nazar aayein.

Pehle fraction ka integral
\[\dfrac{1}{3}\int \dfrac{x}{x^2 + 1}\,dx + \dfrac{1}{3}\int \dfrac{dx}{x^2 + 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{6}\ln(x^2 + 1) + \dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1} x\]
Kyun: Fraction ko do hisson mein toda. \(x\) wala hissa: \(x^2 + 1\) ka derivative \(2x\) hai, is liye \(\frac{1}{2}\) laga kar \(\frac{1}{2}\ln(x^2 + 1)\); \(\frac{1}{3}\) ke saath \(\frac{1}{6}\). Constant wala hissa seedha \(\tan^{-1} x\).

Doosre fraction ka integral
\[\dfrac{1}{3}\int \dfrac{2x}{x^2 + 4}\,dx - \dfrac{1}{3}\int \dfrac{dx}{x^2 + 2^2}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\ln(x^2 + 4) - \dfrac{1}{6}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{2}\]
Kyun: \(2x\) pehle se \(x^2 + 4\) ka poora derivative hai, is liye seedha \(\ln\). Doosre hisse mein \(a = 2\): \(\frac{1}{a}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{a} = \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{2}\), aur \(\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{6}\).
Dhyan dein: \(\int \frac{dx}{x^2 + 4}\) ko \(\tan^{-1} x\) likh dena aam ghalti hai; \(a = 2\) ka asar dono jagah aata hai.

Jawab aur tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{1}{6}\ln(x^2 + 1) + \dfrac{1}{3}\ln(x^2 + 4)\]
\[+ \dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1} x - \dfrac{1}{6}\tan^{-1}\dfrac{x}{2} + c\]
Kyun: Constants ki tasdeeq: \((x + 1)(x^2 + 4) + (2x - 1)(x^2 + 1) = x^3 + x^2 + 4x + 4 + 2x^3 - x^2 + 2x - 1 = 3x^3 + 6x + 3\), jo numerator ka bilkul 3 guna hai (kyunke humne \(\frac{1}{3}\) bahar nikala tha). Sab sahi hai.

blocks.text: Kitab ke aakhir mein answers (page 302) mein Exercise 3.4 ke jawab ghalat heading "Exercise 3.6" ke neeche chhape hain. Is sawal ka jawab us block ka item (xii) hai: \(\frac{1}{6}\ln(x^2 + 1) + \frac{1}{3}\ln(x^2 + 4) + \frac{1}{3}\tan^{-1} x - \frac{1}{6}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{2} + c\). Yeh jawab sahi hai. Jis block par "Exercise 3.4" likha hai (page 301) woh kisi aur exercise ke jawab hain, is liye wahan se milane ki koshish na karein.
